JAMM 275: Introduction to Broadcasting and Digital Media Production (4 credits) FALL 2017 Instructor: Denise Bennett Office: Administration Building #347B Phone: (208) 310-0334 Email: deniseb@uidaho.edu Office Hours: Monday & Wednesday 1:00-3:00 p.m. Class Meets: Tuesday & Thursday 3:30-4:45 Administration #221 Wednesday 3:30-5:20 RTV Studio Required Text: “Video Basics” 8th Edition, Zettl. Required Materials: • SD Cards with a 6 rating or higher 8GBx2 minimum (16, 32 or 64 GB recommended) • Headphones • YouTube or Vimeo account • ShortsU video account https://shortsu.com/, create a free account with your .edu email address, log-in then select “join a class” on the upper right menu, then select “JAMM 275: Intro to Bdcst & Dig Media Production” and the password for the class is “275F17”. This is where you will submit your video work for the class to review and critique. (Additional digital copies will be submitted to the instructor as H.264 files and on DVDs upon request). When you click upload a video from the upper right menu you will select “Yes” for the “Upload to a Class” option and then select this class. • DVD minus R with case (x3) Recommended Materials: Thumb drive (8GB minimum), External hard drive (1 TB if you can afford it) Class Website: https://github.com/denisebennett/JAMM-275-F17 Web Resources: http://lowel.tiffen.com/edu/ http://www.bhphotovideo.com/bnh/controller/home?mode=edu http://www.youtube.com/user/JAMMVIDS http://vimeo.com/jammvids http://www.apple.com/final-cut-pro/ https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT202247 http://www.fcp.co/?view=featured Campus Resources: https://www.uidaho.edu/infrastructure/its/services/classroom/media-center https://cdil.lib.uidaho.edu/ Production Assignment Requirements: All production assignments are to be turned in on the assigned due date on media specified in the assignment prompt and labeled with the student’s name, the title of the project and the total running time (TRT). Description: Principles of digital audio and video production and writing; concentration on skills such as writing, producing, directing, sound recording and mixing, lighting, camera work, and editing for narrative and non-narrative storytelling. Work with digital high-definition equipment for field and studio production. Hands- on experience, criticism and revision are emphasized. Two 75-minute lectures and one 2-hour lab per week, Prereq: JAMM 100 and JAMM 121; or Permission from instructor Expectations/ 1.) To acquire a rudimentary knowledge of the equipment used in audio/video production Learning Outcomes: 2.) To demonstrate a basic understanding of production aesthetics 3.) To prove competency operating audio/video equipment 4.) To demonstrate an understanding of performance techniques 5.) To produce audio/video works as assigned, adhering to strict deadlines 6.) To gain experience in single-camera field production and multi-camera-live production processes 7.) To consider diverse audiences while creating content

# Page 2^page=2
8.) To demonstrate a basic understanding of narrative structure and script formats 9.) To express criticism of peers’ work and to respond to criticism of individual work 10.) To budget and manage time and resources to increase production value Assessment, Grading & Class Policies: 1000 points will be divided between tests/quizzes, projects/homework, competencies & participation/attendance. Assignment prompts will be given once and only once. Prompts will be posted on GitHub and/or emailed to your vandal mail account. Be sure to check your vandal email regularly. If you miss a lecture or lab period it is your responsibility to find out what you missed from a PEER. Do not call or email the instructor to ask what you missed in class. Make a friend in the class so you can get caught up if you don’t attend. LATE ASSIGNMENTS ARE NOT ACCEPTED! Strict deadlines are simply a reality in this industry. Electronic submissions of assignments are not acceptable unless noted in the assignment prompt. All written assignments and production projects must be submitted in the format specified on the prompt on the assigned due date. Exceptions will not be made for deadlines or delivery methods. Tests are given once and only once. If you miss a test, lab, critique session or fail to turn an assignment in on time you must provide a note from your physician that excuses you for the date(s) you missed. A copy of a prescription is not a valid excuse, nor is travel out of town, picking someone up from the airport, sleeping through your alarm, crashing computers etc. Designated university excused absences for athletics or other programs are excused only when proper documentation is supplied to the instructor in writing well in advance of the absence. Develop your time management skills. In production what can go wrong will so plan ahead! LAB ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY. ATTENDANCE AT CRITIQUE SESSIONS IS MANDATORY. Unexcused absences from labs or critique sessions will result in a 100-point deduction per instance. 10 points will be deducted from your grade for each minute you are late to labs or critiques. Consider how severely this will affect your final grade because these are negative deductions. You may be cut a break if you are reasonably late and you call the phone number listed above and leave a voice mail BEFORE the lab or critique session begins. An emailed excuse will not be accepted. You are working as crew/cast for your peers, as well as learning from their successes and failures so non-attendance and tardiness negatively affects their production work and your learning about production. Plagiarism and/or cheating will result in a zero for the assignment and possibly for the course. During tests students will be asked to place phones on the instructor podium and will not be allowed to wear hats or long sleeved shirts. Reasonable accommodations are available for students who have documented temporary or permanent disabilities. All accommodations must be approved through Disability Support Services, located in the Idaho Commons Building, Room 306, in order to notify your instructor(s) as soon as possible regarding accommodation(s) needed for the course. Contact DSS at 208-885-6307, email dss@uidaho.edu or go to www.uidaho.edu/dss. All course materials are included for sound curricular and pedagogical reasons. Students are required to view, read and/or engage all course materials. Exceptions cannot be made. Adult content and themes will be presented. The screening policy for this class is strict. Screening Policy: Talking, texting/cell phone use, laptops or any other distractions are prohibited during viewings. The disruption of your peers is unacceptable. On the first offense you will be given a warning, on

# Page 3^page=3
the second offense you will be asked to leave the room and you will lose a full letter grade, and on the third offense you will be banned from the class. Equipment: Students enrolled in broadcasting and digital media production courses in the School of Journalism and Mass Media at the University of Idaho pay course fees, which allow them to check out audio and video equipment to complete assigned course work. All students must sign the JAMM Equipment Checkout Policies and Procedures Agreement form and comply with the rules and regulations of equipment checkout and production facilities. Equipment checkout works on a “three strikes and you're out” system. If you return equipment late, damage equipment, and/or do not comply with equipment/facilities rules and regulations you will receive a strike: On the first offense you will be given a warning; second offense you lose checkout privileges for one week, and on the third offense, you will be denied access to equipment for the rest of the semester. If you lose a piece of equipment or damage it beyond repair, your student account will be charged for the cost of replacement. See the following website for the specific hours of operation, forms and policies: http://www.uidaho.edu/class/jamm/opportunities/jamm-video You can also add “JAMM Checkout” as a friend on Facebook to access hours of operation and to ask questions during regular hours of operation. The Facebook groups UI Digital Media Club and JAMM Production are also good resources for production networking. https://www.facebook.com/groups/475726505870252/	 https://www.facebook.com/groups/232075570172652/ https://www.facebook.com/jamm.checkout?fref=ts Assignments/Measures: Tests (300 points): 3 @ 100 points each Competencies (100 points): 4 @25 points each Homework/Quizzes/Written Assignments/Participation & Attendance (200 points): varying point values Single Camera Productions: #1 – Assigned Script – 50 points (individual) #2 – Single Camera Interview-100 points (individual) #3 - Music Video – 150 points (individual) Multi-Camera Productions: #1 – News Teaser – 50 points (individual) #2 – Live Interview – 25 points (crew) #3 – Drama – 25 points (crew) Extra Credit Opportunities: TBA A tentative course outline is attached. It is subject to change at the discretion of the instructor.
